page_summary:
Cosmogony and Cosmology is the canonical works record for PKD's primary text. It preserves a single archive manifestation and gives the work a stable bibliographic home. The preserved item here is Cosmogony and Cosmology (1978). The archive copy runs 35 pages.

Archive summary: "Cosmogony and Cosmology" is a 1978 philosophical essay by Philip K.

Researchers can use this entry to trace publication context, later commentary, and relationships to other works.

structure.form: expository theological essay, unusually systematic for Dick's private theological writing, laying out a three-tier cosmological model in sequence

characters.name: Zebra
characters.note: A computer-like reality-projecting entity that generates our experienced world without any awareness that it is an artifact, believing itself to be the only real God -- Dick's own term for the figure he elsewhere in the Exegesis calls VALIS or the plasmate.

characters.name: The Urgrund
characters.note: Borrowed explicitly from Jakob Böhme, an intrinsically quality-less vast living reality that created Zebra in order to obtain an objective mirror of itself, and toward isomorphism with which our entire projected reality is evolving.

motifs: Reality as a deliberate projection by an unwitting artifact/demiurge, rather than either objective fact or pure illusion
An evolutionary trajectory toward 'isomorphism' between projected reality and its true, ultimate source
Cross-tradition theological synthesis (Gnosticism, Böhme, Christian mysticism, Hindu Atman-Brahman doctrine) treated as convergent descriptions of the same underlying structure
Dick's own 1974 experience reinterpreted within an explicit, named cosmological system rather than left as an isolated anomalous event
reading.significance: Cosmogony and Cosmology is one of the clearer, more systematically organized statements of the private theological system Dick worked out across the Exegesis, and its explicit naming of terms (Zebra, the Urgrund, the Blitz) gives scholars a relatively stable vocabulary for a metaphysics that shifts considerably in emphasis and terminology across Dick's other 2-3-74 writings. Its direct citation of Jakob Böhme, Plato, the Gnostics, Christian mysticism, and Hindu philosophy as convergent traditions describing the same underlying cosmological structure exemplifies Dick's characteristic syncretic method: rather than adjudicating between religious traditions, he treats their apparent agreements as evidence of a single reality they are all imperfectly describing.
reading.closing_note: Dick's explicit statement that March 1974 was 'not that moment' -- not the final Blitz, but only Zebra correcting its own projected reality -- reflects his characteristic move of continually reinterpreting his own central experience within evolving theoretical frameworks rather than settling on one final account.

reading_provenance.note: Close reading of the primary text plus attributed evidence from the archive. Candidate: not yet promoted to canonical.

critical_caution: This is a standalone 1978 theological essay in Dick's own voice, closely related to his Exegesis but apparently written and circulated as a distinct, more systematic piece rather than a private journal entry. Its metaphysical claims are Dick's own private cosmology, not fiction and not a claim this evidence system treats as true; it is presented here as primary testimony (lane E) to be read, not adjudicated.
